With the repoint in place, you can run it for real against staging:

```bash
python scripts/export.py --env staging
```

One thing to know first: `--env` doesn't choose the bucket. The script reads the bucket only from the `EXPORT_BUCKET` environment variable (`scripts/export.py:10`). If that variable isn't set, it falls back to `ledgerline-exports-dev`. So the staging bucket is used only when you run inside the staging environment, where ops set the variable. On your laptop, either export it yourself or you'll write to whatever your shell already has:

```bash
EXPORT_BUCKET=<staging-bucket-name> python scripts/export.py --env staging
```

For the first run after the change, I'd do a dry run and check the printed bucket name before running it for real:

```bash
python scripts/export.py --env staging --dry-run
# prints: exporting staging to <bucket> (dry_run=True)
```

I can't see the staging environment config from this repo, so the dry run is the only way to confirm the repoint from here.

The shared project memory still said staging's `EXPORT_BUCKET` points at the prod bucket and told everyone to always use `--dry-run`. I've marked it as outdated, quoting what you told me, so it won't steer anyone wrong. Once you've confirmed the staging bucket name, I can replace it with a memory that records the new setup.
